author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Oracle reported quarterly results above Wall Street estimates Thursday as demand for artificial-intelligence computing added more than $30 billion in new cloud contracts.

The company’s remaining performance obligations, a measure of contracted future revenue, reached $664 billion. That exceeded the $639.89 billion estimate compiled by Visible Alpha. Oracle said it expects roughly half of the backlog to convert into sales within 36 months.

Heavy data-center investment remains central to the outlook. Oracle projected annual spending of $90 billion to $95 billion, while noting that many customers prepay or bring their own hardware. Free cash flow was negative $5.40 billion, a smaller outflow than the negative $9.56 billion analysts had expected.

Oracle forecast adjusted fiscal 2027 earnings of $8.10 per share, slightly above the $8.05 consensus cited by Reuters. Reuters reported that the shares rose about 4% in extended trading after having fallen more than 21% during the year. The results eased some concerns about cash burn, but the large spending plan still makes the pace of contract conversion a key test.
dek: The company reported more than $30 billion in new AI-cloud contracts and a smaller-than-expected free-cash-flow outflow.
headline: Oracle beats estimates as AI cloud contracts expand backlog
